market_holds: Spot $0.8327 at the 2026-11-13 close (Yahoo daily bars, fetched 2026-11-13), 0.4% above the 52-week low and 63% below the high. It is down about 59% year to date (Webull/Simply Wall St piece, 2026-11-02) and has been under $1 since about 2026-10-13. Run-in: -13.6% over 5 sessions and -12.8% over 20. Over the same 5 sessions (11-06 to 11-13) KWEB fell 8.0% and BILI 9.5%, so most of the run-in is the China-internet tape and the stock-specific residual is about -4 to -5 points. The option chain is unusable: no two-sided ATM quotes, open interest 361. The usual move is therefore taken from the last four real earnings prints, all close to close: Nov-2025 +6.3%, Feb-2026 -3.4% (followed by another -6% the next day), May-2026 -2.6%, Aug-2026 -7.5% (followed by a drift to $0.92 by month end). Consensus (Earnings Whispers preview 2026-11-09; Benzinga) is revenue $909M, about -2.6% y/y in USD. At roughly 6.78 RMB/USD (the Q2 release's conversion rate) that is about RMB 6.16B, which is -2% q/q and about -8% y/y in RMB. Consensus EPS is -$0.01 against -$0.04 a year earlier; the whisper is +$0.01. There is no formal guide. Short interest was 70.6M ADS, about 7.3% of shares outstanding, 14 days to cover (FINRA 2026-10-30 via equibles). Since Baidu holds a large block, that is a much larger share of the float. The stock trades on membership revenue and on whether non-GAAP operating income turns positive: the Q2 non-GAAP operating loss was RMB30.3M, and Q3 2025's was RMB21.9M.
view: A shrinking, levered long-video platform with very negative sentiment going into a quarter whose content was mediocre. The Yunhe Q3 2026 report (2026-10-13) shows the quarter's three biggest dramas were all on Youku and Tencent. iQIYI's best exclusives were Zhongqi (Heavy Instrument; #7, 580M effective views) and Quegu (#9, 500M), and its exclusive share of new dramas fell from 61% to 39%. Industry views of the top-20 dramas fell 27% y/y. That points to membership revenue roughly flat q/q, about 4.0-4.1B RMB against 4.21B in Q3 2025, and soft advertising. The same facts point the other way on cost. Fewer exclusives, and fewer titles overall (iQIYI launched 30 new domestic dramas against 33 a year earlier), mean lower content amortisation, so the 'breakeven test' the previews frame (non-GAAP operating income at or above zero) is plausible. My own build: membership ~4.05B + ads ~1.2B + content distribution ~0.5-0.6B + other ~0.35B gives about 6.1-6.2B RMB. That is roughly at consensus, so the revenue line is not where an edge sits. Positioning is crowded short (14 days to cover) and the stock is at its lows. A cost-led beat could squeeze it, as the narrower loss did in Nov-2025 (+6.3%). Against that, three of the last four prints sold off and kept drifting. With a Friday-to-Monday-13:00 window on a sub-$1 ADR with 68% realised vol, weekend China-tape noise alone is several points. I see no line where the price is clearly behind, so this is no call, with a slight lean down because of the weak content quarter and the post-print drift habit.

recommendation.reason: The only fresh independent datapoint, the Yunhe Q3 drama data published 2026-10-13, says iQIYI had a middling content quarter. But consensus already implies about -8% y/y RMB revenue and the stock has fallen about 12% since the data came out, so I cannot show the weak membership quarter is unpriced. The same lighter, less exclusive slate supports a cost-led profitability beat, and a crowded short sits under it. The two pull in opposite directions with no evidence that favours one.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A positive non-GAAP operating income with membership revenue up sequentially (above about RMB 4.1B) would make an up move likely given the short base. Membership below RMB 4.0B with a wider loss, or a going-concern/refinancing warning on the PAG notes (US$522.5M principal, 130% payable at maturity 2028-01-01), would make a sharp drop likely.

self_critique: Down case: the content data is clearly weak for iQIYI relative to Youku/Tencent, and industry views fell 27%. The company has disappointed and drifted lower after three of its last four prints. A second sequential membership decline would break the seasonal excuse management used in Q2. On that reading p_up should be nearer 40. Up case: the stock is at an all-time low with a crowded short, consensus revenue is already low, and cost cuts could deliver the first non-GAAP operating profit in a year. Either reading fits the evidence, which is why I stay near 50.
